recognize_zh: 紅血球彼此邊緣重疊、串成2–3顆的短錢串狀排列（rouleaux），且即使在紅血球分散的薄片區仍可見；畫面中另有兩顆核偏位、細胞質深藍的漿細胞，提示與免疫球蛋白增加（骨髓瘤／漿細胞白血病）相關。
features: Red cells overlapping in short linear stacks of 2-3 cells ('stack of coins') in a thin area of the smear
Unstacked red cells are normocytic and normochromic with preserved central pallor
Circulating plasma cell (lower left) with eccentric round nucleus, clumped chromatin and abundant deeply basophilic cytoplasm
Second plasmacytoid cell (upper) with round nucleus and a rim of pale blue cytoplasm
Scattered small platelets; faint bluish background not clearly appreciable at this magnification
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells aggregating into short linear stacks of two to three cells in an otherwise thin area, while isolated red cells are normocytic and normochromic. Two circulating plasmacytoid cells are present, including one with an eccentric nucleus, coarse chromatin and abundant basophilic cytoplasm. No red cell agglutinates (irregular clumps) are seen. Findings are consistent with rouleaux formation with circulating plasma cells, in keeping with plasma cell myeloma/plasma cell leukemia.

ddx.vs: Agglutinates form irregular three-dimensional clumps rather than linear coin stacks and disperse on warming, whereas rouleaux disperse with saline dilution.
In thick smear areas overlap is random and nonlinear, whereas true rouleaux persist as linear stacks in the thin feathered edge.
Also causes rouleaux but circulating cells are mostly plasmacytoid lymphocytes with IgM paraprotein; separation requires immunofixation, flow cytometry and MYD88 L265P testing.
